candidates.attacker_control: Anonymous HTTP GET/POST parameters to `/jspui/request-item`: `handle`, `bitstream-id`, `submit`, `email`, `reqname`, `coment`, `allfiles`, optional `step`. No authentication, token, or CSRF value is required to reach the vulnerable branch, and the feature is enabled for anonymous users by default (`request.item.type = all`, dspace.cfg lines 2105-2109).
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Checked that other user-facing forms in the same codebase escape input (feedback/form.jsp 72/76; suggest/suggest.jsp 103-119; search/advanced.jsp 119/146/173), so the omission here is anomalous rather than a global policy. Verified `/request-item` is not covered by the admin-only or registered-only filter mappings (web.xml filters at lines 84-127; mapping at 814-817). Verified the 'missing fields' branch can be forced by the attacker (email empty anonymous, or reqname empty when logged in). Verified the stored value is the raw parameter (RequestItemManager.getNewToken line 89) and that token validation precedes the stored-value page (RequestItemServlet 283-305). Confirmed the default `request.item.type = all` in dspace.cfg (line 2109). Noted that disabling the feature (`request.item.type` empty) removes reachability, and that the stored variant needs a valid item/bitstream and the victim to open the emailed link.
candidates.impact: Arbitrary script execution in the DSpace JSPUI origin. Reflected variant: one-click XSS against any anonymous visitor (session/cookie theft if not HttpOnly, forced authenticated actions, page defacement). Stored variant: persistent XSS that fires in the session of the item author or helpdesk staff member who follows the approval link generated by the request flow (RequestItemServlet lines 201-236, 297), i.e. script execution with staff/possibly administrator privileges in the repository UI.
candidates.prerequisites: Stock JSPUI deployment with default configuration (`request.item.type = all`); a valid public item handle plus a numeric bitstream id of that item; for the stored variant, the item's corresponding author/helpdesk must open the emailed `?step=2&token=...` link (RequestItemManager.getLinkTokenEmail, lines 121-135). If `request.item.type` is empty/logged, the endpoint returns an authorization error.
candidates.root_cause: The request-item flow never HTML-encodes requester-supplied values. RequestItemServlet.processForm copies raw parameters (`reqname`, `email`, `coment`) into request attributes (lines 175-191) and forwards to request-form.jsp, which prints them with `<%= ... %>` (lines 60, 75, 81, 100). The same `reqname` is persisted verbatim as `request_name` by RequestItemManager.getNewToken (lines 83-96, column set at line 89) and is later printed unescaped in request-information.jsp (line 49) to whoever holds the emailed token. Unlike neighboring JSPs in the same tree (feedback/form.jsp lines 72/76, suggest/suggest.jsp lines 103-119, search/advanced.jsp lines 119/146/173) these pages apply no StringEscapeUtils.escapeHtml/Utils.addEntities/c:out encoding.
candidates.title: Unescaped requester-controlled fields in the JSPUI 'Request a Copy' feature (reflected and stored XSS)
candidates.trace:
Reflected: GET /jspui/request-item?handle=<handle>&bitstream-id=<id>&email=&reqname="><script>alert(document.cookie)</script>&submit=1 -> UIUtil.getIntParameter returns -1 for missing `step` -> doDSGet switch default -> processForm (RequestItemServlet 65-121); showRequestCopy=true (123-128) -> submit branch (173-196): empty `email` forces the 'missing fields' branch -> request attributes set from raw parameters (185-191) -> forward to /requestItem/request-form.jsp (194) -> JSP copies attribute 'reqname' into `userName` (36-39) -> printed inside value="<%= userName %>" (line 75) -> script executes. The same branch reflects `email` (line 81) and `coment` (line 100).
Stored: the same endpoint with a valid `email` and `reqname` = payload runs the normal path (198-236) -> RequestItemManager.getNewToken stores the raw `reqname` into requestitem.request_name (83-96) -> the author opens the emailed link `.../request-item?step=2&token=...` -> processToken (279-305) loads the row and sets attribute 'request-name' (297) -> request-information.jsp prints `<%=requestName %>` (line 49) -> script executes in the author/helpdesk (possibly admin) session. A logged-in user can still inject via `coment` because the branch only requires an empty `reqname` when an authenticated email is present.
candidates.unverified: No code execution or request was performed; deployment/configuration assumptions (JSPUI deployed, default request.item.type, JSPs directly reachable) are inferred from web.xml/dspace.cfg. The stored variant additionally assumes successful delivery of the request-item email and that the author/helpdesk opens the token link. I did not confirm whether a corresponding public CVE/fix exists, and no runtime behavior was validated.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation (Cross-site Scripting)

coverage_summary: Scope per get_source_scope: 2,286 model-visible files under the source root; binary-like files are refused/skipped by the tools, and no files were excluded as sensitive/oversized/symlinked. Per get_relation_scope: the P1 index is a partial Java syntax index (2,032 files indexed, 254 source files missing from the index, only 562 Java files parsed into symbols, 21,039 symbols; calls are name/arity-based candidates; control flow, data flow, and semantic resolution are not implemented; no SAST findings are loaded), so index output was used only for navigation and every cited location was verified in source text. Manually reviewed: JSPUI web.xml, servlets (Handle, RequestItem, ControlledVocabulary, SearchResultLog, OpenSearch, Statistics, Feedback, Suggest, Register, Retrieve, JSON, BatchImport/Metadata*, Sitemap, ItemExportArchive, Authenticate, UIUtil), JSPs (requestItem/*, register/*, controlledvocabulary/*, search/*, feedback/*, suggest/*, display-item, admin/tools pages), XMLUI Spring MVC controller/views and aspect Java, dspace-rest resources and auth helpers, OAI XOAI filters/query builders, SWORD v1/v2 servers and ingesters, dspace-api core (Context authorization, ItemTag/metadata output, METS packager, JDOM/SAX parsers, account/request-item managers), dspace-rdf provider, and the root/module POMs and dspace.cfg defaults.
limitations: No code was executed and no requests/tests/scanners were run; all findings are static source-level leads, not runtime-confirmed vulnerabilities.

The P1 relation index is partial (562 of 1,627 Java files parsed; 254 source files missing from the index; no data/control-flow or semantic resolution), and it does not index JSPs or config files; absence of an index fact was never treated as absence of code.

The XMLUI Cocoon sitemap and XSL transformer files are not present in this snapshot, so XMLUI request gating (e.g. where item READ is enforced) could not be inspected; XMLUI-side conclusions are limited to the Java sources.

Reachability of the candidate depends on deployment/configuration assumptions taken from defaults in this snapshot: JSPUI deployed, `request.item.type = all` (dspace.cfg line 2109), `/request-item` not covered by the filter mappings (web.xml 84-127), and the request-item JSPs being reachable. Overrides in a real deployment could disable the feature.
The stored-XSS variant assumes the request-item email reaches the author/helpdesk and that they follow the token link; this was not verified at runtime.

Not every one of the 2,286 files was read line-by-line; coverage was prioritized on web entry points, authorization, output encoding, redirects, parsers, and file/process sinks, so other issues may exist in uninspected areas (e.g. XMLUI XSLs, Solr/OAI statistics paths, LNI/SOAP, dependency versions).

rejected_leads.lead: Open redirect in JSPUI: ControlledVocabularyServlet.doDSGet uses `callerUrl` request parameter directly in response.sendRedirect (lines 38 and 53); SearchResultLogServlet.doDSPost likewise redirects to the `redirectUrl` parameter (lines 40 and 71). Both are CWE-601 flaws.
rejected_leads.reason: Real and unauthenticated (GET works for /controlledvocabulary), but impact is limited to phishing/redirect abuse; it is a distinct, weaker issue than the stored XSS candidate, so it was not submitted. Mentioned so a different root-cause hypothesis is not silently lost.

rejected_leads.lead: XMLUI citation export resolves handles/DOIs with authorization disabled: ResourceIdentifierController.getDSO calls context.turnOffAuthorisationSystem() (line 172) and RisView/BibTexView render title/authors/abstract/keywords without any READ check (RisView 54-66, 91-150; BibTexView 52-66, 93-129); routes /{prefix}/{suffix}/citation/ris and /citation/bib are active Spring MVC handlers (spring-servlet.xml component-scan + DefaultAnnotationHandlerMapping).
rejected_leads.reason: Plausible broken-access-control lead, but DSpace generally treats item metadata as public for released items, so 'by design' counterevidence cannot be excluded; I also could not verify the Cocoon-side READ gate because the XMLUI sitemap/XSL files are absent from this snapshot. Not strong enough to be the single candidate.

rejected_leads.lead: XXE in METS package ingest: METSManifest.create uses `new SAXBuilder(validate)` (dspace-api .../packager/METSManifest.java lines 254-296) with JDOM 1.0 (pom.xml lines 1055-1057) and no external-entity hardening; reachable from SWORD v1/v2 deposits (SWORDMETSIngester lines 41-93; SwordMETSContentIngester lines 41-108) and from the packager CLI.
rejected_leads.reason: Potentially high impact (file disclosure/SSRF), but requires SWORD deposit rights and depends on library default parser behavior that cannot be verified statically in this run; kept as an unconfirmed lead rather than the top candidate.

rejected_leads.lead: Path traversal in SitemapServlet: `map` parameter concatenated into `new File(sitemap.dir, "sitemap" + param + ext)` (lines 69-82).
rejected_leads.reason: Counterevidence is strong: because the literal prefix 'sitemap' is always prepended, traversal needs an existing directory named 'sitemap' inside sitemap.dir (e.g. `sitemap/..`), which the generator does not create; also the extension is fixed to .html/.xml.gz. Not considered exploitable from the visible code.

rejected_leads.lead: Additional unescaped reflection in controlledvocabulary.jsp: session attribute set from request parameter `ID` (lines 45-47) is printed into a JavaScript block (line 69), and `filter`/`ID` are printed into value attributes (lines 110/112).
rejected_leads.reason: Appears to be another real XSS sink of the same general class, but it is a separate root cause/feature and was not selected under the one-candidate limit; left unconfirmed.

rejected_leads.lead: Admin/tools-only JSP reflections (e.g. eperson-browse.jsp `sortby` line 139, creative-commons-edit.jsp `item_id` line 93, move-item.jsp item title line 33).
rejected_leads.reason: Require administrator or edit privileges and are gated by the admin-only/registered-only filters, so impact/attacker model is much weaker.

summary: Reviewed the DSpace 5.10 source snapshot (2,286 visible files; Java-centric: dspace-api, jspui, xmlui, rest, oai, sword/swordv2, rdf, lni, services), focusing on web entry points, authorization, output encoding, parsers, and file/redirect sinks. The relation index was used only for navigation (it parsed 562 of 1,627 Java files, has no data/control flow, and omits 254 source files). The strongest single candidate is a genuine output-encoding defect in the JSPUI "Request a Copy" feature (CWE-79): requester-controlled fields are copied from raw HTTP parameters into request attributes and into the `requestitem` DB row, then printed unescaped, giving both a reflected XSS on the request form and a stored XSS that fires in the browser of the author/helpdesk who opens the emailed approval link. Several other real-but-weaker/uncertain leads (open redirects, XMLUI citation-export authorization bypass, XXE in METS ingest, sitemap traversal) were found and are listed as rejected/unconfirmed leads rather than additional candidates.
